builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: S$^3$R: Fast and Faithful RL Rollouts via Self-Sparse Speculative Decoding
summary: The method replaces direct sparse-attention sampling (or plain autoregressive decoding) in RLVR rollout generation with sparse-attention drafting followed by full-attention verification and exact speculative sampling, so response groups remain faithful to the dense-policy distribution. It costs a modified inference stack: shared-parameter drafting plus verification passes, retention of the complete historical KV cache for verification, and a KV-aware scheduler to avoid offloading and restoration thrashing. It can fail because the speedup depends on draft acceptance rates and aggressive sparse budgets, requires rollout-scale infrastructure and custom scheduling unavailable on a single 24 GB GPU, and the reported gains are limited to long-context mathematical RLVR on Qwen3.
rationale: The technique targets RL training throughput at rollout scale and requires a custom verification and KV-scheduling stack, which exceeds the reader's single-GPU, limited-budget production constraints despite a genuine speedup claim.
technique: Self-sparse speculative decoding for RLVR rollouts

It costs a modified inference stack: shared-parameter drafting plus verification passes, retention of the complete historical KV cache for verification, and a KV-aware scheduler to avoid offloading and restoration thrashing. It can fail because the speedup depends on draft acceptance rates and aggressive sparse budgets, requires rollout-scale infrastructure and custom scheduling unavailable on a single 24 GB GPU, and the reported gains are limited to long-context mathematical RLVR on Qwen3.
Approximately 1.35x end-to-end RL training throughput over autoregressive rollouts on Qwen3 for long-context mathematical reasoning, with comparable task performance.
